passages.text: This is the third time I am coming to you. “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul says, “This is the third time I am coming to you.”
Paul teaches a rule.
Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
passages.original: Τρίτον τοῦτο ἔρχομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς Ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων καὶ τριῶν σταθήσεται πᾶν ῥῆμα

passages.text: I already warned you the second time I was with you. So now in my absence I warn those who sinned earlier and everyone else: If I return, I will not spare anyone, since you are demanding proof that Christ is speaking through me. He is not weak in dealing with you, but is powerful among you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the one speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul already warned them when he visited the second time.
Now Paul is absent from them.
Paul warns those who sinned earlier.
Paul also warns everyone else in the church.
If Paul returns again, he will not spare anyone.
The people are demanding proof that Christ speaks through Paul.
Christ is not weak in dealing with them.
Christ is powerful among them.
passages.original: Προείρηκα καὶ προλέγω ὡς παρὼν τὸ δεύτερον καὶ ἀπὼν νῦν τοῖς προημαρτηκόσιν καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς πᾶσιν ὅτι ἐὰν ἔλθω εἰς τὸ πάλιν οὐ φείσομαι ἐπεὶ δοκιμὴν ζητεῖτε τοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ λαλοῦντος Χριστοῦ ὃς εἰς ὑμᾶς οὐκ ἀσθενεῖ ἀλλὰ δυνατεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν

passages.text: For He was indeed crucified in weakness, yet He lives by God’s power. And though we are weak in Him, yet by God’s power we will live with Him to serve you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ was crucified.
He was crucified in weakness.
God raised Him by His power.
Now Jesus lives by the power of God.
We are also weak in Jesus.
But God will give us life with Jesus.
God’s power will work in us.
We will live with Jesus by God’s power.
God’s power will help us serve you.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐσταυρώθη ἐξ ἀσθενείας ἀλλὰ ζῇ ἐκ δυνάμεως Θεοῦ καὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς ἀσθενοῦμεν ἐν αὐτῷ ἀλλὰ ζήσομεν σὺν αὐτῷ ἐκ δυνάμεως Θεοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Can’t you see for yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you—unless you actually fail the test?
passages.sermon:
You must examine yourselves.
You must see if you are truly in the faith.
You must test yourselves.
You must recognize if Jesus Christ is in you.
If you do not see Christ in you, you have failed the test.
passages.original: Ἑαυτοὺς πειράζετε εἰ ἐστὲ ἐν τῇ πίστει ἑαυτοὺς δοκιμάζετε ἢ οὐκ ἐπιγινώσκετε ἑαυτοὺς ὅτι Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν εἰ μήτι ἀδόκιμοί ἐστε

passages.text: And I hope you will realize that we have not failed the test.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter to the Corinthians.
Paul and his companions serve as apostles of Jesus Christ.
Paul expresses hope.
He hopes the Corinthians will understand something important.
He wants them to realize that he and his companions have not failed the test of faith.
passages.original: ἐλπίζω δὲ ὅτι γνώσεσθε ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἐσμὲν ἀδόκιμοι

passages.text: Now we pray to God that you will not do anything wrong—not that we will appear to have stood the test, but that you will do what is right, even if we appear to have failed.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
Paul and his companions pray to God for the believers.
They pray that the believers will not do anything wrong.
Paul does not pray this so that he and his companions will appear approved.
Paul prays this so that the believers will do what is right.
Paul and his companions are willing to seem unapproved if the believers do what is right.
passages.original: Εὐχόμεθα δὲ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν μὴ ποιῆσαι ὑμᾶς κακὸν μηδέν οὐχ ἵνα ἡμεῖς δόκιμοι φανῶμεν ἀλλ’ ἵνα ὑμεῖς τὸ καλὸν ποιῆτε ἡμεῖς δὲ ὡς ἀδόκιμοι ὦμεν

passages.text: For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
Paul and his companions serve God.
Paul and his companions always support the truth.
Paul and his companions cannot act against the truth.
Paul and his companions can only act for the truth.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ δυνάμεθά τι κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας

passages.text: In fact, we rejoice when we are weak but you are strong, and our prayer is for your perfection.
passages.sermon:
We are apostles of Jesus Christ.
We feel joy when we are weak.
We see that you are strong.
We pray for you.
We ask God to make you complete.
passages.original: χαίρομεν γὰρ ὅταν ἡμεῖς ἀσθενῶμεν ὑμεῖς δὲ δυνατοὶ ἦτε τοῦτο καὶ εὐχόμεθα τὴν ὑμῶν κατάρτισιν

passages.text: This is why I write these things while absent, so that when I am present I will not need to be severe in my use of the authority that the Lord gave me for building you up, not for tearing you down.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul writes this letter while he is not with the Corinthians.
Paul writes these things for a reason.
He wants to avoid being severe when he visits them in person.
The Lord gave Paul authority.
The Lord gave this authority to Paul to build up the church.
The Lord did not give this authority to Paul to tear the church down.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ταῦτα ἀπὼν γράφω ἵνα παρὼν μὴ ἀποτόμως χρήσωμαι κατὰ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἣν ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκέν μοι εἰς οἰκοδομὴν καὶ οὐκ εἰς καθαίρεσιν

passages.text: Finally, brothers, rejoice! Aim for perfect harmony, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christian brothers and sisters in Corinth.
He tells them to rejoice.
He tells them to aim for perfect harmony.
He tells them to encourage one another.
He tells them to be of one mind.
He tells them to live in peace.
God is the God of love and peace.
God will be with them.
passages.original: Λοιπόν ἀδελφοί χαίρετε καταρτίζεσθε παρακαλεῖσθε τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖτε εἰρηνεύετε καὶ ὁ Θεὸς τῆς ἀγάπης καὶ εἰρήνης ἔσται μεθ’ ὑμῶν

passages.text: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to the Christian brothers and sisters in Corinth.
He told them how to act toward each other.
He said, "Greet one another."
He said, "Do this with a holy kiss."
A holy kiss shows love and respect among believers.

passages.text: All the saints send you greetings.
passages.sermon: All the saints greet you.\r\nThe saints are God’s holy people.\r\nThey send their greetings to you.

passages.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.
passages.sermon:
The Lord Jesus Christ gives grace.
God shows love.
The Holy Spirit brings fellowship.
I pray these blessings will be with all of you.
passages.original: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἡ κοινωνία τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν
